L28: ## Quick search
L29: 
L30: Your search will be quickest if you narrow it down as much as possible. Wide searches are unlikely to get results and may cause your session to time out. For search tips, refer to 【5†Search criteria】 below.
L31: 
L32: 【10†Search our records now(opens in a new window)†my.rio.bdm.vic.gov.au】
L33: 
L34: or read the tips below before you start.
L35: ## Ask a Family History expert
L36: 
L37: Need help? Our genealogy experts can help with your search or do it for you.
L38: 
L39: Generally, fees start at $65.30, depending how many people you want us to search for. Each package includes at least one certificate image.
L40: 
L41: Learn more about 【9†inclusions and fees for Ask a Family History expert】.
L42: 
L43: To Ask an Expert:
L44:   * Email your request to bdmdatarequests@dgs.vic.gov.au(opens in a new window)
L45:   * Include the person’s:
L46:     * Name (surname and first name). Let us know if you’re unsure about the spelling. We’ll check minor variations
L47:     * Date and place of birth, death or marriage
L48:     * Any other relevant details.
L49: 
L50: Our genealogy experts will contact you within a week to discuss.
L51: 
L52: Alternatively, you can try your own search above.
L53: ## Not all records are available for searching
L54: 
L55: Records are restricted for between 30 and 100 years, depending on the life event. Family history search lets you search for records that fall outside this period. Refer to 【11†Periods of restriction】.
L56: 
L57: The restriction is from the date the event was registered. This may not be the same as the date of the event.
L58: If you're looking for a record inside the restriction period, go to 【12†Get a birth certificate】, 【13†Get a marriage certificate】 or 【14†Get a death certificate】.
L59: 
L60: Death records are kept secure for 30 years. If you’re looking for a friend or family member who recently died, it won’t be available here. You may be able to access it if you’re next of kin: refer to 【14†Get a death certificate】.
L61: ## 1. Choose a search index
L62: 
L63: Choose the index you want to search by selecting 'Historical' or 'Events at sea'.
L64: 
L65: [Button: Open all]
L66: 
L67:   * What's in the Historical index?
L68: 
L69: The historical index holds the following life events registered in Victoria.
L70: Date ranges for the historical records we hold
L71: Life event  | From  | To
L72: --- | --- | ---
L73: Births  | 1853  | 100 years before today's date
L74: Marriages and relationships  | 1853  | 60 years before today's date
L75: Deaths  | 1853  | 30 years before today's date
L76: Church baptisms, marriages and burials  | 1836  | 1853
L77: 
L78: Records become available on the day they reach the end of their restriction period.
L79: 
L80: Example: you search for a birth registered on 12 April 1919. If you conduct your search:
L81:     * Before 12 April 2019, you won't find it
L82:     * On or after 12 April 2019, it is available to find.
L83: 
L84: This is because the restriction period for births is 100 years.
L85: 
L86:   * What's in the Events at sea index?
L87: 
L88: Births, deaths and marriages on ships bound for port in Victoria, between 1853 and 1920.
L89: 
L90: Each entry in the historical and event at sea indexes includes the:
L91:     * Name of the person or people the entry relates to
L92:     * Type of event (e.g. birth, marriage or death)
L93:     * Name of the ship (if applicable)
L94:     * Registration year and number
L95:     * Other information relevant to the type of event.
L96: ## 2. Search criteria
L97: 
L98: Enter your search criteria and click search. We recommend:
L99: 
L100:   * Using a first and last name, if possible
L101:   * Entering a 5-year timeframe. This allows for differences between event registration and year of event
L102:   * Keeping the timeframe narrow (e.g. around 5 years). A wide timeframe may make your results slow to come back or not work at all. You can refine the range if your first search gets no results.
L103: 
L104:   * Can't find what you're looking for?
L105: If you can't find the entry, try using:
L106:     * Different criteria combinations (or fewer criteria)
L107:     * Different spellings or abbreviations of names (for example, Wm instead of William)
L108:     * An asterisk (*) after a letter. This will search for all entries beginning with those letters (for example, W* or Wil*)
L109:     * Leave out 'place of event' if you're unsure or having trouble finding your entry. It is a tricky search criterion as historical records often used an abbreviation.
L110:     * Consider using our ‘Ask an expert’ service. Our genealogy experts can do the search for you.
L111: ## 3. View record summary
L112: 
L113: Click on an entry to see the summary for that record. You can access the full record, if you choose to, after payment.
L114: ## 4. Buy the record
L115: 
L116: You'll be given two options at the bottom of the record screen. To buy, click 'add to cart' and 'checkout' to proceed with payment.
L117: Historical records, purposes and prices
L118: Product  | Purpose  | Price
L119: --- | --- | ---
L120: Uncertified historical certificate (a scanned image of a certificate)  | This isn't valid for official purposes. You're simply buying a scanned image of an official record.If you buy an uncertified image, you can download it immediately.  | $20.00
L121: Historical certificate  | This is valid for official purposes. If you choose to buy, you'll be prompted to fill in your details. We will post the certificate to you.  | $59.10
L122: ## 5. Download an image
L123: 
L124: Once you've bought an image, we will email you a link and you can download it straight away.
L125: 
L126: Each image is a scan of the original – often handwritten – record. Over time, some have faded or suffered damage, and may not be easy to read. We've tried hard to capture the best possible image of each record.
L127: 
L128: Download your image within 30 days of purchase.
L129: 
L130: If you have trouble downloading it, check your computer and browser firewalls and security settings. Then try again.

Wągrówieckie.

 Dnia 11. listopada 1918 r. po poł. przeniosła się rewolucja do miasta Wągrówca. 12. listopada zajęli się organizacją rewolucji Marjan Chmielewski, adwokat Hilary Ewert i Mieczysław Kajkowski. W handlu M. Kajkowskiego przy rynku utworzono natychmiast biura werbunkowe dla wracających wojaków z pola i o godzinie 10½ przed poł. [152]zapisało się już 250 polskich żołnierzy. Od rana opanowano pocztę i stację kol. i zwołano w przeciągu przedpoł. prawie wszystkich polaków z okolicy. O godz. 11-tej przed południem wybrano wykonawczy komitet rewolucyjny, który się składał z 12 polaków i 6 niemców. Na czele tego komitetu stanął Marjan Chmielewski. Na rynku zebrały się wielkie tłumy ludu, do którego przemówił p. Tadeusz Grabowski ze Zbietki, podnosząc, że wreszcie okowy pruskie pękły i gwiazda wolności ludom przyświeca. Very much loved Opa of Rebecca, Robert, Max, Ebony, Tori, Marcus and Stella. Loved Great Opa to their children. Always in our hearts and loved forever.
